comparison: Both evaluate sample size and study design (C2, C17, C129, C130) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval additionally addresses ethical approval claims (C131, C132) not mentioned in peer review. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the large sample size as a major strength, fully aligning with OpenEval's assessment.

Perfect alignment on developmental trajectory claims (C3, C4, C25, C32, C33, C85). Both rate as SUPPORTED with strong endorsement. Peer reviewers described findings as 'clear and compelling,' matching OpenEval's assessment of consistent statistical support across age bins.

Complete agreement on exploration and motor noise findings (C5, C18, C19, C35, C45, C46, C47). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed the modeling findings showing 'increases in exploration' and 'reduction of intrinsic motor noise,' directly confirming OpenEval's evaluation.

Strong alignment on task manipulation effects (C6, C20, C51, C56, C57, C62, C63, C66, C67). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses 9 claims including statistical details (C64, C65 not in peer review), while peer reviewers focus on 9 overlapping claims. Both affirm that discrete/deterministic manipulations rescued younger children's performance.

Perfect agreement on baseline motor competence claims (C21, C22, C26, C89, C90). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted that deficits were not due to basic motor control issues, consistent with OpenEval's assessment that baseline performance data support the inference about learning deficits.

Complete alignment on age-related baseline precision improvement (C30, C31). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted this finding as part of 'reduced movement variability' developmental changes without challenge, matching OpenEval's positive assessment.

Perfect agreement on clamp condition variability findings (C34, C36, C37). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers affirmed these as part of the overall developmental pattern showing 'increases in exploration,' consistent with OpenEval's assessment of reasonable inference from age-dependent patterns.

Complete alignment on model selection approach (C38, C39, C40, C92). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the extensive model comparison with BIC penalization, directly confirming OpenEval's assessment of strong evidence for model selection.

Perfect agreement on model fit quality (C48, C50). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers affirmed the modeling as 'very strong' and accepted the explanatory power without criticizing the modest variance explained, matching OpenEval's assessment.

Complete alignment on discrete task findings (C52, C53, C54, C55, C58, C59). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted these results as part of the experimental manipulation showing task simplification rescued performance, consistent with OpenEval's positive evaluation.

Perfect agreement on in-lab validation (C79, C80, C81, C82). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly praised 'in-lab replications' as reflecting 'laudable rigor,' directly confirming OpenEval's assessment of validated online data collection.

Complete alignment on task comprehension evidence (C83, C84, C87, C91). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted that basic reinforcement learning mechanisms are present in young children, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of converging evidence for task understanding.

Divergence in certainty level. OpenEval rates interpretation of spatial/probabilistic processing limitations (C88, C112) as SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'still needs more direct evidence.' Peer reviewers used cautious language ('suggesting') rather than definitive claims.

Perfect agreement on kinematic differences (C27, C28, C29). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted these descriptive findings without concern as part of the overall developmental characterization, matching OpenEval's assessment.

Complete alignment on remote study limitations (C122, C123, C124, C125). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledged limitations but noted in-lab validation addressed concerns, consistent with OpenEval's assessment that authors appropriately acknowledged limitations while providing mitigating evidence.

Both address control analyses showing no confounding effects. OpenEval covers C60, C61, C68 as SUPPORTED; peer review addresses C68, C69, C70, C71, C75, C76 as SUPPORTED. Minimal overlap (C68 only) but both affirm the control analyses and statistical decomposition of effects.

Partial overlap on clamp condition effects. OpenEval addresses C69, C70, C71, C72, C73, C74 as SUPPORTED; peer review addresses C68, C69, C70, C71, C75, C76 as SUPPORTED. Both affirm differential effects in clamp conditions, though OpenEval includes mechanistic interpretations (C72, C73, C74) not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on task manipulation effects on model parameters. OpenEval addresses C75, C76 as SUPPORTED; peer review addresses C68, C69, C70, C71, C75, C76 as SUPPORTED. Both affirm the differential effects on motor noise versus exploration variability.

Agreement on uncertainty level. OpenEval rates cognitive mechanism speculation (C103, C104, C105, C106) as UNCERTAIN; peer review rates C103, C104, C106 as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'still needs more direct evidence.' Both recognize these claims as speculative interpretations not directly tested in the study.

OpenEval evaluated model mechanics description (C41, C42, C43, C93, C94) as SUPPORTED, noting these are direct descriptions of the selected model structure. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific model description claims.

OpenEval evaluated model predictions and optimal behavior claims (C77, C78, C97, C98) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate distinction between predicted and observed behavior. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these theoretical model prediction claims.

OpenEval evaluated exploration behavior findings with supporting citations (C99, C100, C101) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about convergent evidence from other motor tasks.
